newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND'S AWS GAINS ON RULING LEFT AFTER FLOOD-POLL.
newsitem.headline: POLAND'S AWS GAINS ON RULING LEFT AFTER FLOOD-POLL.

text.p: A July poll by the public CBOS
institute showed the co-ruling ex-communist Democratic Left
Alliance (SLD) lost two points to the opposition Solidarity
Electoral Action (AWS) two months before general elections.
The SLD kept its lead with 24 percent of votes with AWS
right at its heels with 23 percent, according to the July 24-30
poll, published on Monday.
CBOS said 68 percent of Poles declared they would cast
their vote in the parliamentary polls on September 21 but that
the real turn-out was likely to be lower.
The institute said the changes in voter preference, small
enough to fall within the range of statistical error, showed
that July's disastrous floods in the south of the country have
not yet been fully comprehended by Poles.
"It seems the main political effect of the floods is, so
far, an increase in the number of undecided voters. One can say
that a large number of Poles still does not realise what
happened in July in the south of Poland," the report said.
Poland's opposition has accused the government of delay and
mismanagement in its handling of the crisis. Political analysts
say this may have a bearing on the ruling coalition's election
performance, but the full picture will take time to emerge.
The government denies that it was at fault, blaming the
unexpected scale of the disaster for any problems in rescue and
relief efforts.
Following are five most recent public opinion surveys by
leading polling agencies.

NOTE - Party names: AWS - The Solidction, an
opposition electoral bloc of more than 30 small right-wing
parties led by the Solidarity trade union.
SLD - the Democratic Left Alliance, the ex-communist group
and the larger partner in the ruling leftist coalition.
PSL - The Polish Peasant Party, the smaller partner in the
government coalition.
UW - The Union for Freedom, a right-centrist group, the
biggest opposition party in parliament.
ROP - The Movement for Reconstruction of Poland, a
non-parliamentary group, advocating patriotic, anti-communist
and often populist values.
UP - The Union of Labour, a leftist opposition party.
KPEiR - The National Pensioners' Party, a party lobbying
for pensioners' interests.
Polling agencies: CBOS - public, Poland's biggest polling
institution. OBOP - controlled by state-owned television.
DEMOSKOP - private. PBS - private, prepares polls for
Rzeczpospolita daily.
